title: Uniform interpolation and forgetting in classical propositional logic

based_on.title: Interpolation in Classical Propositional Logic (arXiv:2508.11449v3, July 6, 2026)
based_on.pages: §4 pp.6–7 and §7 pp.11–12; §9.1 pp.15–17 only for the resolution connection

summary: Forget selected atoms by constant substitution, retaining every consequence in the remaining vocabulary and obtaining its dual universal factor.
abstract: An implication chain from p to q and from q to r entails p implies r. If we stop mentioning q, which other consequences remain available? A single formula can retain all of them: replacing q by false and by true, then joining the results with a disjunction, preserves exactly the assignments that can extend to satisfy the original formula. Repeating this finite construction gives uniform interpolation, where the middle formula is chosen before any future consequence is supplied. We prove its vocabulary and extension properties, obtain classical deduction factors and the dual universal construction, and connect the result with clause elimination by resolution.
